name: Aljamain Sterling
event: UFC Fight Night: Procházka vs. Stirling
summary: Former UFC bantamweight champion (26-5, age 37), now 3-1 at featherweight after wins over Brian Ortega and Youssef Zalal. An elite back-taking grappler who wins mostly on the scorecards. Featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski says Sterling deserves the next title shot if he beats Kevin Vallejos (Sherdog).

how_they_fight.Striking: Long, kick-heavy outside game. Used leg kicks to chop Ortega's lead leg and won almost every exchange in a low-output fight (Cageside Press). He is accurate (58%) but not powerful: only three KO/TKO wins and about 0.04 knockdowns per 15 minutes. Mostly uses striking to set up takedowns.
how_they_fight.Grappling: The main weapon. About 2.8 takedowns per 15 minutes and a third of total fight time in control. Against Zalal he went 6 for 11 on takedowns with almost 14 minutes of control, took the back, used a body triangle and won 49-45 x3 (LowKick MMA). Against Kattar: 8 of 13 takedowns and almost 11 minutes of control. Eight submission wins, but none since 2020 (Sandhagen).
how_they_fight.Defense: Both knockout losses came against fast power punchers: Marlon Moraes R1 (2017) and Sean O'Malley R2 (2023). His other three losses were decisions (Caraway, Assuncao, Movsar Evloev). He was caught in a tight guillotine by Zalal in R3 and lost top position that round (LowKick). Takedown defense is average (60%).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: A grinder who goes the distance: 14 of 26 wins are decisions, and he is 6-1 in five-round fights (the loss was the O'Malley KO). His last stoppage win was in 2022 (Dillashaw, R2). At featherweight all three wins went 15 or 25 minutes. He holds his pace into rounds four and five (dominant R4-R5 against Zalal), but in the Ortega fight he faded into R5, where Ortega clipped him and he was warned for retreating (Cageside).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Smart, patient, takes few risks. Gave Ortega a pause after a disputed eye poke when he might have pushed for a finish (Cageside). Has publicly accepted Vallejos's call for a 'pure striking' fight, which would mean leaving his best weapon behind if he means it.

patterns: Leg kicks and range work to set up takedowns
Back-taker: body triangle and hand-fighting for the choke
Wins on the cards: 14 decisions in 26 wins, no finish since 2022
Loses when caught by fast power punchers (Moraes, O'Malley)
concerns: Little power at 145 against a heavy hitter
Knocked out twice by explosive strikers
keys_to_beat: Keep it standing and make him eat counters on entries
Defend the first takedown and get back up fast; do not give the back
Punish level changes with knees and front headlock threats

news.text: Says the UFC gave him one hour to accept Vallejos; he turned down Aaron Pico because Vallejos made more sense for his title case (Heavy.com).
Replied 'Can't wait!' to Vallejos predicting a 'pure striking' fight.
Volkanovski said Sterling deserves the next shot at 145 if he beats Vallejos, and Jean Silva if not.
Criticised referee Dan Miragliotta's stand-up in the Moicano-Nolan main event; Vallejos joked he'd been promised Miragliotta as referee.
